answer: A mechanism that actually bites: attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because basalt only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, harbor is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any knoll approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
